fix(decisions): a status line travels, so it may not name a location (S54)

rules why prints a record's Status: line into whatever repository the reader is
standing in, and most of them are repositories that adopted simt-dev and own
none of this package's files. Five records wrote "affects src/resolve/resolve.mjs"
into it. The review measured two and called it pre-existing; the corpus says five,
and three of them were written after that measurement - ADR-041, then ADR-053 and
ADR-054 in this cycle. A finding that grows while it is being fixed is a finding
whose cause is a convention, and the convention is ADR-038's own: Affects: is the
field for a location, five records had one available, and Status: is the line the
tool reads - which is exactly why putting it there was wrong.

The ruling covers Status: and deliberately not the record's argument. docs/plans/
means this package's plan in one record and the adopting repository's own plans in
another, test/leaks.mjs already singles that string out as a substitution default
that is correct for the reader, and four records use it for both. Redacting prose
would have to guess, and a guessed redaction makes a correct sentence wrong. Seven
records still print a location in prose and a test asserts the count and the ids,
so the decision is visible rather than an unmeasured shrug.

Redaction happens once in loadDecisions, so the text command, the JSON payload and
the MCP surface cannot disagree about what a record says. The exempt list - three
top-level files plus every dot-entry - is asserted against a real simt-dev init,
because a claim about a set held in a comment is a value nobody executes.

The summarise docstring's promise is withdrawn rather than left standing: it
asserted a property of prose the function never had, which is ADR-049 one level
down, a sentence that reads like evidence and carries none.
